headings: Our operating results, our ability to execute on our strategy and the carrying value of our assets are exposed to the effects of volatile commodity prices or prolonged periods of low commodity prices.
If we do not successfully develop resources, the scope of our business will decline, and our financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected.
The exploration and production of oil and gas is a highly competitive industry.

Our ability to successfully execute on our plans to reduce operational GHG emissions intensity is subject to a number of risks and uncertainties and such reductions may be costly and challenging to achieve.
Our ability to manage risk or influence outcomes in joint ventures may be constrained.
Our operations are subject to hazards and risks that require significant and continuous oversight.
We expect to continue to incur substantial capital expenditures and operating costs as a result of our compliance with existing and future environmental laws and regulations.
Broader investor and societal attention to and efforts to address global climate change may limit who can do business with us or our access to financial markets and could subject us to litigation.
Political and economic developments could damage our operations and materially reduce our profitability and cash flows.
Political and economic factors in international markets could have a material adverse effect on us.
Other Risk Factors Facing our Business or Operations
We may need additional capital in the future, and it may not be available on acceptable terms or at all.
Our business may be adversely affected by deterioration in the credit quality of, or defaults under our contracts with, third parties with whom we do business.
Our ability to execute our capital return program is subject to certain considerations.
There are substantial risks with any acquisitions or divestitures we have completed or that we may choose to undertake.
Our technologies, systems and networks are subject to cybersecurity threats.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors in addition to the other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. These risk factors are not the only risks we face. Our business could also be affected by additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently consider to be immaterial. If any of these risks or other risks that are yet unknown or currently considered immaterial were to occur, our business, operating results and financial condition, as well as the value of an investment in our common stock, could be materially and adversely affected.

Among the most significant factors impacting our revenues, operating results and future rate of growth are the sales prices for crude oil, bitumen, LNG, natural gas and NGLs. These prices are tied to market prices that can fluctuate widely due to factors beyond our control. For example, over the course of 2025, WTI crude oil prices ranged from a high of $80 per barrel in January to a low of $55 per barrel in December. Given the volatility in the drivers of commodity prices and our associated realizations, the worldwide political and economic environment, including potential economic slowdowns or recessions, unexpected shocks to supply and demand, or increased uncertainty generated by armed hostilities and geopolitical tension and escalations in various oil-producing regions around the globe, prices for crude oil, bitumen, LNG, natural gas and NGLs may continue to be volatile.

Prolonged periods of low commodity prices could have a material adverse effect on our revenues, operating income, cash flows and liquidity, and may also affect the amount of dividends we elect to declare and pay on our common stock and the amount of shares we elect to acquire as part of our share repurchase program and the timing of such repurchases.

Lower prices may also limit the amount of reserves we can produce economically, thus adversely affecting our proved reserves and reserve replacement ratio and accelerating the reduction in our existing proved reserve levels as we continue production from upstream fields. Prolonged depressed prices may affect strategic decisions related to our operations, including decisions to reduce capital investments or curtail operated production.

Significant reductions in crude oil, bitumen, LNG, natural gas and NGLs prices could also require us to reduce our capital expenditures, impair the carrying value of our assets or discontinue the classification of certain assets as proved reserves. Although it is not reasonably practicable to quantify the impact of any future impairments or estimated change to our unit-of-production rates at this time, our results of operations could be adversely affected as a result.

As we produce crude oil, bitumen, natural gas and NGLs from our existing portfolio, the amount of our remaining reserves declines. If we do not successfully replace the resources we produce with good prospects for future organic development or through acquisitions, our business will decline. In addition, our ability to successfully develop our reserves depends on our achievement of a number of operational and strategic objectives, some aspects of which are beyond our control, including navigating political and regulatory challenges to obtain and renew rights to develop and produce hydrocarbons; reservoir optimization; bringing long-lead time, capital intensive projects to completion on budget and on schedule; and efficiently and profitably operating mature properties. If we are not successful in developing the resources in our portfolio, our financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected.

It should be read in conjunction with the financial statements and notes, and supplemental oil and gas disclosures included elsewhere in this report. The terms "earnings" and "loss" as used in Management's Discussion and Analysis refer to net income (loss).
Business Environment and Executive Overview

ConocoPhillips is one of the world's leading E&P companies, based on both production and reserves, with operations and activities in 14 countries. Our diverse, low cost of supply portfolio includes resource-rich unconventional plays in North America; conventional assets in North America, Europe, Africa and Asia; global LNG developments; oil sands in Canada; and an inventory of global exploration prospects. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, at December 31, 2025, we employed approximately 9,900 people worldwide and had total assets of $122 billion.

At ConocoPhillips, we anticipate that commodity prices will continue to be cyclical and volatile, and our view is that a successful business strategy in the E&P industry must be resilient in lower price environments while also retaining upside during periods of higher prices. As such, we are unhedged, remain committed to our disciplined investment framework and continually monitor market fundamentals, including the impacts associated with geopolitical tensions and conflicts, global demand for our products, oil and gas inventory levels, governmental policies, inflation and supply chain disruptions.

Throughout 2025, the price of crude oil has been volatile due to multiple macroeconomic and geopolitical forces which slowed global oil demand growth concurrent with higher oil production from OPEC Plus and other major oil producing countries. We continue to closely monitor the macroeconomic environment, including any impacts from tariffs, and the ongoing market volatility in the energy landscape and across global markets for implications to our business, results of operations and financial condition.

As the global energy industry continues to evolve, we remain committed to creating long-term value for our stockholders. We believe ConocoPhillips plays an essential role in responsibly meeting the global demand for energy, while continuing to deliver competitive returns on and of capital and working to meet our previously established emissions-reduction targets. Our value proposition to deliver competitive returns to stockholders through price cycles is guided by our foundational principles, which consist of maintaining balance sheet strength, providing peer-leading distributions, making disciplined investments, and demonstrating responsible and reliable ESG performance.

Total company production in 2025 was 2,375 MBOED, yielding cash provided by operating activities of $19.8 billion. We invested $12.6 billion into the business in the form of capital expenditures and investments and provided returns of capital to shareholders of $9.0 billion through our ordinary dividend and share repurchases. In 2025, we returned $4.0 billion through the ordinary dividend, inclusive of an increase in December of eight percent to 84 cents per share. In addition, we returned $5.0 billion to shareholders through share repurchases. As of December 31, 2025, we have repurchased $39.3 billion of shares of our authorized share repurchase program since 2016. In February 2026, we declared a first-quarter ordinary dividend of 84 cents per share.
ConocoPhillips 2025 10-K Management's Discussion and Analysis

In November 2024, we completed our acquisition of Marathon Oil. In the first half of 2025, we completed the asset integration of Marathon Oil and by year-end 2025 achieved more than $1 billion of synergies on a run-rate basis and approximately $1 billion of one-time benefits. These one-time benefits include $0.5 billion recognized previously upon close of the transaction related to the utilization of foreign tax credits, with the remainder related to cash tax benefits from net operating losses, most of which was recognized in 2025. See Note 3.

Separately, in the second half of 2025, we announced incremental cost reductions and margin enhancements of more than $1 billion anticipated on a run-rate basis by year-end 2026. In late 2025, we initiated a restructuring, reducing our overall employee workforce, which in addition to lease operating cost improvements and opportunities in transportation and processing is expected to contribute approximately $0.8 billion in cost reductions. We anticipate the remaining approximately $0.2 billion to be achieved through margin expansion.

In August 2025, we announced a total disposition target of $5 billion by year-end 2026. We disposed of $3.2 billion of assets in 2025 and we expect to meet our $5 billion disposition target by year-end 2026. Completed dispositions to date include the Ursa and Europa fields and Ursa Oil Pipeline Company LLC for net proceeds of $0.7 billion, the Anadarko Basin for net proceeds of $1.2 billion and other noncore Lower 48 and Corporate assets for approximately $1.3 billion. See Note 3.

As part of our LNG strategy to build a dynamic portfolio and expand our footprint across the value chain, we have various commercial LNG offtake agreements in North America totaling 10.2 MTPA with offtake commencing between 2026-2031. Furthermore, we currently have a total regasification capacity in Europe of approximately 6.7 MTPA. We continue to progress discussions across all major LNG producing and consuming regions and markets to further add high-quality positions to our portfolio.

Operationally, we remain focused on safely executing the business while also progressing key strategic initiatives. At Willow, we made significant progress and achieved critical milestones, successfully completing our largest winter season. In the Lower 48, we integrated Marathon Oil assets into our portfolio, focusing on operating and capital efficiencies. Internationally, we became the sole operator of the Kebabangan Cluster (KBBC) PSC in Malaysia in January 2025, extending the PSC to 2050 and making KBBC our first operated producing asset in Malaysia. In Canada, we achieved first oil at Surmont Pad 104W-A in December 2025. Additionally, our equity LNG projects continued to advance at NFE and NFS in Qatar and PALNG on the U.S. Gulf Coast.

paragraphs: 管理階層的討論與分析為本公司對其財務表現及可能影響未來表現的重大趨勢與不確定性之分析。應與財務報表及附註、以及本報告其他處所包含的補充油氣揭露資訊一併閱讀。內容包含前瞻性陳述，包括但不限於本公司所做出之計畫、策略、目標、預期與意圖等陳述，係根據1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案之「安全港」條款所作出。詞彙如「抱負」、「預期」、「相信」、「預算」、「持續」、「可能」、「努力」、「估計」、「預期」、「預測」、「目標」、「指引」、「意圖」、「可能」、「目標」、「展望」、「計畫」、「潛力」、「預測」、「預測」、「追求」、「應該」、「目標」、「將」、「會」及類似詞彙，用以識別前瞻性陳述。本公司不承諾更新、修訂或更正任何前瞻性資訊，除非根據聯邦證券法有此義務。讀者應謹記，這些前瞻性陳述應與本公司於「為1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案之「安全港」條款用途之警示聲明」標題下所披露資訊一併閱讀，該部分自第62頁開始。
在管理階層的討論與分析中所使用的「獲利」及「虧損」一詞，係指淨收入（虧損）。
營運環境與執行摘要
康菲石油公司為全球領先的探採石油與天然氣（E&P）公司，根據產量與儲備量而言，其業務遍及14個國家。我們多元化的低成本供應組合包含北美地區資源豐富的非常規油氣田；北美、歐洲、非洲及亞洲的傳統資產；全球液化天然氣（LNG）開發項目；加拿大油砂；以及全球探勘潛力的存貨。總部設於德克薩斯州休士頓，截至2025年12月31日，我們在全球僱用約9,900名員工，總資產為1220億美元。
在康菲石油公司，我們預期原油價格將持續呈現週期性與波動性，我們的觀點是，在探採石油與天然氣產業中，成功的商業策略必須在低價環境中具備韌性，同時在高價時期也能保留上漲潛力。因此，我們未進行套期保值，持續致力於我們嚴謹的投資架構，並持續監測市場基本面，包括與地緣政治緊張與衝突、全球對我們產品的需求、油氣存貨水平、政府政策、通貨膨脹及供應鏈中斷相關的影響。
2025年期間，原油價格因多項總體經濟與地緣政治因素而波動，這些因素同時減緩了全球油氣需求成長，並伴隨著OPEC Plus及其他主要油氣生產國的油氣產量增加。我們持續密切監測總體經濟環境，包括關稅的影響，以及能源領域及全球市場的持續市場波動，以評估對我們業務、營運成果與財務狀況的影響。
隨著全球能源產業持續演進，我們仍致力於為股東創造長期價值。我們相信康菲石油公司在負責任地滿足全球能源需求方面扮演關鍵角色，同時持續提供資本與運營的競爭性回報，並努力達成我們先前設定的減碳目標。我們透過價格週期為股東提供競爭性回報的價值主張，是以我們的基礎原則為導向，這些原則包括維持強健的資產負債表、提供業界領先的分紅、進行嚴謹的投資，以及展現負責任且可靠的ESG表現。

2025年本公司總體產量為2,375 MBOED，產生營運活動產生之現金為198億美元。我們在2025年投入126億美元用於資本支出與投資，並透過普通股息與股票回購向股東回饋90億美元。2025年，我們透過普通股息回饋40億美元，包含12月提高8%至每股0.84美元。此外，我們透過股票回購回饋股東50億美元。截至2025年12月31日，自2016年起，我們已透過授權股票回購計畫回購價值393億美元的股票。2026年2月，我們宣佈第一季普通股息為每股0.84美元。
ConocoPhillips 2025 10-K 管理層討論與分析
2024年11月，本公司完成對Marathon Oil的收購。2025年上半年，本公司完成Marathon Oil資產整合，並於2025年底達成逾10億美元的節省效益（按年化計算）及約10億美元的一次性效益。這些一次性效益包括於交易完成時已認列的5億美元，與外國稅收抵免的使用有關，其餘則與淨運營虧損所產生的現金稅務效益有關，其中大部分已在2025年認列。詳見附註3。
另外，2025年下半年，本公司宣佈預計於2026年底達成逾10億美元的增量成本削減及邊際提升（按年化計算）。2025年底，本公司啟動一項重整計畫，減少整體員工人數，加上租賃營運成本改善及運輸與處理的機會，預計將貢獻約8億美元的成本削減。本公司預期剩餘約2億美元將透過邊際擴張達成。

2025年8月，本公司宣佈至2026年底總計處分資產目標為50億美元。2025年本公司已處分價值32億美元的資產，並預期於2026年底達成50億美元的處分目標。截至目前為止已完成的處分包括Ursa與Europa油田及Ursa Oil Pipeline Company LLC，淨現金收入為7億美元；Anadarko盆地，淨現金收入為12億美元；以及其他非核心Lower 48及企業資產，約為13億美元。詳見附註3。
根據本公司LNG策略，以建立動態投資組合並擴展價值鏈的足跡，本公司在北美地區擁有總計10.2 MTPA的商業LNG銷售協議，銷售開始時間為2026至2031年間。此外，本公司目前在歐洲的總再氣化容量約為6.7 MTPA。本公司持續進行與所有主要LNG生產與消費地區及市場的討論，以進一步增加高品質的投資組合位置。

從營運方面而言，本公司持續專注於安全執行業務，同時推進關鍵戰略計畫。在Willow，本公司取得重大進展並達成關鍵里程碑，成功完成最大規模的冬季作業。在Lower 48地區，本公司將Marathon Oil資產整合至投資組閤中，專注於營運與資本效率。國際方面，本公司於2025年1月成為馬來西亞Kebabangan Cluster (KBBC) PSC的唯一經營者，將PSC期限延長至2050年，並使KBBC成為本公司在馬來西亞的第一個經營生產資產。在加拿大，本公司於2025年12月達成Surmont Pad 104W-A的首次開採。此外，本公司在卡塔爾NFE與NFS以及美國墨西哥灣沿岸PALNG的權益LNG專案持續推進。

headings: 與我們產業相關的風險
本公司營運成果、執行策略的能力以及資產的帳面價值，會受到商品價格波動或長時間低商品價格的影響。
若我們未能成功開發資源，本公司業務範圍將縮小，且財務狀況與營運成果可能受到不利影響。
石油與天然氣的探勘與生產屬於高度競爭的產業。
本公司執行減少運營溫室氣體排放強度計畫的能力，受到許多風險與不確定性影響，且此類減少可能成本高昂且難以實現。
本公司管理風險或影響合資企業結果的能力可能受到限制。
本公司營運受到危害與風險影響，需要進行持續且重大的監督。
我們預期將持續產生大量資本支出及營運成本，這是因為我們必須遵守現行及未來的環境法規與法律。
更廣泛的投資人與社會對全球氣候變遷的關注及努力解決此問題，可能會限制與我們交易的對象或我們對金融市場的接觸，並可能使我們面臨訴訟風險。
政治與經濟發展可能損害我們的營運，並大幅降低我們的獲利與現金流。
國際市場的政治與經濟因素可能對我們產生重大不利影響。
其他影響我們業務或營運的風險因素
我們未來可能需要額外資金，且可能無法在合適的條件下或完全無法取得。
我們的業務可能因與我們交易的第三方信用品質惡化或其與我們的契約發生違約而受到不利影響。
我們執行資本回報計畫的能力受到某些因素的影響。
本公司進行任何收購或出售交易均存在重大風險。

paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮下列風險因素，並配合本年度報告書（Form 10-K）中包含的其他資訊。這些風險因素並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。我們的業務也可能受到其他尚未為我們所知或目前認為不重要的風險與不確定性影響。若任何這些風險或其他尚未知或目前認為不重要的風險發生，將可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況，以及投資本公司普通股的價值造成重大且不利的影響。

影響我們營收、營運結果與未來成長率的最重要因素之一，為原油、瀝青、液化天然氣（LNG）、天然氣與天然氣液體（NGLs）的銷售價格。這些價格與市場價格相關，而市場價格可能因超出我們控制範圍的因素而大幅波動。例如，在2025年期間，西德克薩斯中質原油（WTI）價格從1月的每桶80美元高點，降至12月的每桶55美元低點。考慮到商品價格驅動因素的波動性與我們相關的實現情況，以及全球政治與經濟環境，包括潛在的經濟減速或衰退、供應與需求的意外衝擊，或因武裝衝突與地緣政治緊張與各油氣生產區的升級而產生的增加不確定性，原油、瀝青、液化天然氣（LNG）、天然氣與天然氣液體（NGLs）的價格可能持續波動。
長時間的低商品價格可能對我們的營收、營運收入、現金流與流動性造成重大不利影響，也可能影響我們決定發放並支付普通股股息的金額，以及我們決定透過股票回購計畫購回股票的數量與時間。
較低的價格也可能限制我們能經濟性生產的儲備量，因此對我們的已證實儲備與儲備替換率造成不利影響，並加速我們現有已證實儲備水平的減少，隨著我們持續從上游油田進行生產。長時間的低價可能影響我們的運營決策，包括減少資本投資或削減經營生產的決策。
原油、瀝青、液化天然氣（LNG）、天然氣與天然氣液體（NGLs）價格的重大下降，也可能迫使我們減少資本支出、減損資產的帳面價值，或停止將某些資產歸類為已證實儲備。儘管目前尚無法合理量化任何未來減損或預估單位生產率變動的影響，但我們的營運結果可能因此受到不利影響。

隨著我們從現有資產組閤中生產原油、瀝青、天然氣與天然氣液體（NGLs），我們的剩餘儲備量會減少。若我們未能成功以具有良好未來有機發展潛力的資源或透過收購來替換所生產的資源，將導致我們的業務衰退。此外，我們能否成功開發儲備，取決於我們達成多項運營與戰略目標的能力，其中一些方面超出我們的控制範圍，包括應對政治與法規挑戰以取得並續期開發與生產氫碳化合物的權利；儲層最佳化；將長期、高資本需求的項目按預算與時程完成；以及高效且獲利地運營成熟資產。若我們未能成功開發資產組閤中的資源，將可能對我們的財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。
